ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council. Time donations are not permitted during Oral Communications. Please submit a â€œWHITEâ€ speaker slip to the City Clerk. If at least two (2) Council Members agree, direction may be given to staff to put an item on a future agenda or provide additional information to answer a question.

CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a â€œPINKâ€ speaker slip to the City Clerk. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Council Member or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar.
8A.
Approval of the Warrants List. Contact Person: Finance Manager Lundgren
Approve the Warrants.
2016-05-18 Item 08A Warrants
8B.
Proposed installation of a Little Free Library Box on a City trail easement. Contact Person: Acting Park Superintendent Stauffer
That the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute a License Agreement, as approved by the City Attorney, for installation of a Little Free Library Box on a City trail easement.
2016-05-18 Item 08B Little Free Library
8C.
The renewal of the Encinitas Landscape and Lighting District. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Ruess
1) Adopt City Council Resolution No. 2016-48 (Attachment 1), resolution of intention to order the renewal of the Encinitas Landscape and Lighting District for FY 2016-17; and 2) Set the public hearing for June 8, 2016.
2016-05-18 Item 08C Renewal Encinitas Landscape and Lighting District
8D.
Legislative Position Letter. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst McSeveney
Approve the legislative position letter for the Mayorâ€™s signature.
2016-05-18 Item 08D Legislative Position Letter
8E.
Resolution No. 2016-40 establishing all-way stop control at the intersection of Melba Road and Evergreen Drive. Contact Person: Traffic Engineer Blough
Staff recommends that Council adopt Resolution No. 2016-40 (Attachment 1) establishing an all-way stop at the intersection of Melba Road and Evergreen Drive.
2016-05-18 Item 08E Melba and Evergreen All-Way Stop
8F.
Sixth Amendment to Streetlight Attachment Agreement with Crown Castle NG West, LLC. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst McSeveney
1) Consent to one five-year extension to the existing Streetlight Attachment Agreement with Crown Castle NG West, LLC as allowed in the original agreement dated July 24, 2006; 2) Approve the Sixth Amendment to Streetlight Attachment Agreement for Telecommunications Facilities with Crown Castle NG West, LLC; and 3) Authorize the City Manager to execute said Sixth Amendment.
2016-05-18 Item 08F Crown Castle NG West Agreement
9.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR Staff reports will be given only if requested by the person who pulled the item.
The title of ordinances listed on this agenda are deemed to have been read and further reading waived.
10.
ACTION ITEMS
10A.
Consideration of the Rail Corridor Vision Study Professional Services Agreement. Contact Person: Acting Director of Planning and Building Ranu
Staff recommends that Council adopt Resolution No. 2016-59 authorizing the City Manager: a) to enter into an agreement for professional services with WSP ' Parsons Brinckerhoff to undertake the Rail Corridor Vision Study (WC15A); b) to refine the scope of work to achieve the project goals and provide for coordinated public engagement between the Rail Corridor Vision Study, Active Transportation Plan and Parking Study; and c) to report back to Council on the final scope of work for the Rail Corridor Vision Study, final scope of work for the Parking Study and any amendments made to the Active Transportation Plan.
2016-05-18 Item 10A Rail Corridor Vision Study
10B.
Review and consideration of the proposed ten year-extension of the expiration date for Housing Certification Program (HCP) units and the proposed one year extension of the Interim Provisions of the Affordable Unit Policy (AUP) program. Contact Person: Principal Planner Langager
Staff recommends that Council take the following actions: 1) Extend the expiration date for all existing HCP units an additional ten years to June 16, 2026; 2) Extend the Interim Provisions of the AUP program an additional year to June 16, 2017; 3) Direct staff to pursue legislative relief at the state level for flexibility in applying the uniform construction codes to illegal units appropriate for legalization; and 4) Direct staff to return at a future date with a work plan to address options to promote affordable housing and incentives to legalize unpermitted housing units.
2016-05-18 Item 10B Affordable Unit Policy
10C.
Proposed 2017 Major Special Events review and selection. Contact Person: Management Analyst Crystal Roff
Council review and authorize proposed 2017 Major Special Events.
2016-05-18 Item 10C 2017 Major Special Events
10D.
Encinitas Community Park One-Year update. Contact Person: Interim Director Parks and Recreation Oâ€™Grady
Receive the report and provide direction to Staff as regarding future projects within Encinitas Community Park.
2016-05-18 Item 10D Encinitas Community Park One Year Report

ADJOURNMENT - THE NEXT REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING WILL BE HELD ON MAY 25, 2016
Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
